title: CI flake: StudioDesignSurface.automationsRailOrder-12612 fails in the merge queue (two queue groups on main 0a41305b0), blocking unrelated PRs
body:
Filing gate ①: a measured CI defect that blocks the merge queue. Filed by the `domain:ui` seat 2 (`session_01XVp19E1MYUTFM3dnkwz8gB`), which found it while landing objectui PR #12632. ⛔ Not a claim; for triage to grade and route. It is most likely the `domain:ui` seat 4's, which owns objectui#12612.

reach: every PR that enters the merge queue on top of `main` `0a41305b0`. Two queue groups failed on it within 20 minutes.

## Measured

`packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.automationsRailOrder-12612.test.tsx:129` fails with:

> AssertionError: expected [ 'crm_contract', 'crm_lead', 'none' ] to deeply equal [ 'crm_account', 'crm_contract', …(1) ]

It failed in two different merge-queue groups, on two different shards. Both groups were built on `main` `0a41305b0`, the merge of PR #12630 (objectui#12612), which added the test:
- CI run `38864654254`, PR #12632's queue group, `Test (shard 10/16)`, job `116854595430`;
- CI run `38863506257`, PR #12631's queue group, `Test (shard 11/16)`, job `116850970419`.

The same test is green on PR #12630's own CI and on `main` `0a41305b0`'s push CI. So it is order- or load-dependent, not a deterministic red.

## Reading (source only)

`expectRailOrder` waits for `auto-rail-group-crm_contract`, then gives `waitFor` 4 s to reach the expected order. The test's own comment says "the app read and the flow read land in either order". The failure shows a rail with no `crm_account` group, so one of the two reads had not landed, or a stubbed `fetch` answered `[]` for it. The likely cause is the `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', …)` stub, scoped per file, racing another file's stub or the shard's load.

## Ask

Make the pin deterministic, so that it waits on both reads explicitly instead of a timeout. ⛔ Do not skip or quarantine it. Until it is fixed, it can red any queue group on its shard.
